title: (Invited Paper) AnaFlow: Agentic LLM-based Workflow for Reasoning-Driven Explainable and Sample-Efficient Analog Circuit Sizing
problem: Analog circuit sizing remains a handcrafted, time-consuming process prone to errors, requiring excessive simulation cycles and lacking explainability in automated approaches.
motivation: Automating analog design with explainability and sample efficiency enables faster iteration and wider adoption of AI-driven circuit design tools.
method: Multi-agent LLM workflow interprets circuit topology and design goals, iteratively refines parameters via adaptive simulation strategy that learns from optimization history. Agents provide human-interpretable reasoning at each step.
key_novelty: LLM-agent-based framework for sample-efficient analog sizing with inherent explainability, adapting simulation strategy based on prior optimization mistakes.
contributions: Agentic LLM workflow for circuit topology interpretation and design goal understanding
Adaptive simulation strategy for high sample efficiency
Learning mechanism that avoids past mistakes and accelerates convergence
Explainable design space exploration tool for analog circuit optimization

metrics.speedup: fully automatic completion vs. Bayesian optimization/RL approaches
metrics.accuracy: successful on two circuits of varying complexity

limitations: Evaluation limited to two circuit examples; scalability to complex multi-block designs not demonstrated.
primary_theme: agentic LLM for explainable analog design
